posts.sub: The three labels overlap more than they differ. Here is what each one names, and which to use with your buyers.
posts.brief: Verdict first: say AEO to buyers, mention GEO so you match what they search, keep SEO for Google work. Link: AEO vs SEO (Oct 9).
covers: What SEO, AEO and GEO each name, in a table.
Where the term GEO came from (a 2023 research paper).
Why the label matters less than the target: being named in the answer.
posts.learn: AEO, GEO and SEO are mostly one job under different names. The real shift is that fewer people click through when an AI answer is on the page.

data.text: Google: "There are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, nor other special optimizations necessary." Also: "You don't need to create new machine readable files, AI text files, or markup", and "no special schema.org structured data that you need to add". SEO best practices remain relevant.
data.source: Google Search Central, AI features and your website (updated 2025-12-10)

data.text: Pew: with an AI summary, people clicked a regular result link in 8% of visits, against 15% with no summary. They clicked a link inside the summary in 1% of visits. 26% of pages with a summary ended the browsing session, against 16% without. 58% of respondents had at least one search with an AI summary; 18% of all searches produced one.
data.caveat: 900 US adults, 68,879 Google searches, March 2025. Observational. Google only. Panel of people who installed tracking software.

data.text: The GEO paper (Aggarwal et al., first submitted 2023-11-16, accepted to KDD 2024): "GEO can boost visibility by up to 40% in generative engine responses."
data.caveat: "Up to" is an upper bound. The benefit varies by domain. "Visibility" is defined inside the paper's framework.

data.text: SparkToro: 68.01% of US Google searches ended without a click in January to April 2026 (Similarweb desktop and mobile web panel), against 60.45% in 2024 (Datos panel). SparkToro says the rise is "almost certainly driven by the massive growth in AI Overviews".
data.caveat: The two years use different panels (SparkToro calls it "apples and oranges"). Excludes the Google mobile app. The data does not isolate AI Overviews as the cause.

judgment: The verdict (say AEO to buyers, mention GEO, keep SEO) is our judgment, not a sourced fact.
ask: Do you want AiM to commit to "AEO" as its main term?
Is "mention GEO once so you match searches" right for how you want AiM to sound?

A one-hour plan in order.
Why copy comes first.
posts.learn: Google's own position on special AI files and markup, and why plain page text comes first.

data.text: Google: "There are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, nor other special optimizations necessary." Also: "You don't need to create new machine readable files, AI text files, or markup", and "no special schema.org structured data that you need to add". SEO best practices remain relevant.
data.source: Google Search Central, AI features and your website (updated 2025-12-10)

data.text: Vercel (December 17, 2024): "none of the major AI crawlers currently render JavaScript." OpenAI's and Anthropic's crawlers fetched JavaScript files (11.50% and 23.84% of requests) but did not run them. Google's Gemini and Apple's AppleBot did render JavaScript.
data.source: Vercel blog, The rise of the AI crawler
data.caveat: A December 2024 snapshot from Vercel's own network and nextjs.org. Crawler behaviour changes. Vercel's labels are "ChatGPT" and "Claude", which may not map exactly to GPTBot and ClaudeBot.

data.text: SE Ranking, about 300,000 domains: 10.13% had an llms.txt file (9.88% low traffic, 10.54% mid, 8.27% high). "There's no correlation between AI citations and LLMs.txt." Removing it from their model improved the model's accuracy.
data.caveat: Authors say results are context-dependent and may be outdated within weeks. Secondary coverage dates the study November 2025; the date on the page is unresolved.

data.text: llms.txt was proposed by Jeremy Howard, published September 3, 2024. The site says the AI labs publish llms.txt for their own developer docs (it names OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini). It does not say their products read other sites' files.

judgment: The ordering (copy, then markup, then llms.txt) is our reading of the evidence.
Crawler behaviour and study findings are snapshots; the post says so.
